description: Line 59 compares the untrimmed c.status with 'CLOSED'. SQL Server ignores trailing spaces and, under the usual collation, case, but it does not ignore leading spaces. A status such as ' CLOSED' passes the <> 'CLOSED' test, so claims closed long ago (or with no closed_date) still make the list. They then appear as 'CLOSED' because the output column is trimmed (INC-3204).

impact.query: SELECT COUNT(*) AS rows_affected, COALESCE(SUM(incurred_amount),0) AS amount_affected FROM golden_rpt_large_loss_watchlist WHERE claim_status = 'CLOSED' AND (closed_date IS NULL OR closed_date <= DATE'2025-10-02')

intended_behaviour: Use the same cleaned status in the filter as in the output: UPPER(LTRIM(RTRIM(c.status))) <> 'CLOSED'. Closed claims would then stay only if closed_date > @PriorDate.
title: CLOSED check uses the raw status, not the trimmed one
